sentence_stem: If I had known about the traffic,
correct_completion: I would have left home earlier.
full_sentence: If I had known about the traffic, I would have left home earlier.
acceptable_variants: I would have taken the train instead.
I could have avoided the delay.

options.text: I will leave home earlier tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: 'Will' refers to the future, but the stem sets up a hypothetical past situation that did not happen, which needs a past modal form.

options.text: I left home at seven o'clock.
options.why_wrong: This is a simple statement of a past fact; it does not complete the conditional, which needs 'would have' plus a past participle.

options.text: I would have left home earlier.
I must leave home earlier every day.
options.why_wrong: 'Must' expresses present obligation, which does not match the hypothetical past situation introduced by 'if I had known'.

grammar_focus: Third conditional with a modal perfect (would have + past participle)
explanation: After 'if I had known', the result clause must describe what would have happened in the past, so 'would have' plus a past participle is required. Learners may find this hard because some languages express the same idea with a single conditional marker and no separate perfect modal form.
translation: Trafiği bilseydim, evden daha erken çıkardım.
